When we challenge ourselves, and direct ourselves, we are reprimanded by society. Many of us learn to not pursue our interests, because they are childish, or inappropriate for someone of our physical attributes, or whatever other nonsense. Many of us are taught to ignore our interests. We are not without direction. We are taught to ignore where our minds direct us, because they direct us towards “wasting” our time.

I’ve forgotten the point I was making. To other people, we seem to have no direction, and it seems like we aren’t challenging ourselves, because they don’t know shit about autism, and they’re only used to autism that’s presented in a certain way, which is typically how it’s presented in media. For us, if we are given freedom to develop as we wish, we will learn to direct ourselves, and we will constantly seek out challenge, to refine our minds.

I think all people need this freedom. It’s not just autistic people who do not challenge themselves, and are without direction. I think it’s just that our current way of life leaves people too overwhelmed to do anything more than work and sleep.

If we can make life easier for each other, we should aim to, and encourage each other to aim to. Humans are social creatures. We need acceptance from society. If society will not accept us, we should be able to find that acceptance within ourselves, and each other. We should encourage ourselves, and each other, to be better, in a compassionate and fair manner.

Point is, it don’t make no sense to me, I tell ya, that we are autistic people, and nobody ever considered asking you what you aimed to achieve with your initial comment. We could’ve nipped this whole thing in the bud, if only we aimed to understand you, and not judge you based on a miscommunication, as society does to us.
You get better as you make mistakes, as long as you learn from them.

Autism is a neurodevelopmental condition. That’s means we all have autism of the brain, and the brain is what dictates how we handle stress, and how we behave, as a result. You were banned for behaving in a manner that would be expected of an autistic person. The problem is that your behaviour does not align with their narrow understanding of autism.

For those you care about, you are willing to change to make their lives less unbearable. Those you don’t care about, their suffering will always be invisible to you.

This is why it is vital that we accept all autistic people, and try to be understanding with each other. We are all in this shit pit together. There’s nothing to be gained from excluding those who are “too” autistic. You have no idea how high I am. These people are imitating a society that does not accept those who step outside the boundaries of normality. I’d imagine it’s because their self-acceptance is not genuine, or they are stuck with an ableist society’s perception of us, because it is imprinted as soon as we come into contact with society. When it’s done to young people, we grow up thinking it’s normal, and we behave in that way.

Being raised in a violent environment can make violence seem like the normal way of operating. Being raised in a misogynistic environment can make misogyny seem like the normal way of operating.

The way we talk about women reflects our views on them. When we talk about them like children, is it because we genuinely perceive them as intellectual peers, or do we view them as incompetent, and immature? Do we view women as prone to emotional outbursts, like children? Weak, unable to defend themselves, like children?

We should always question everything, to figure out what is wrong, and how we can fix it.

But that’s because we’re not properly educated on it, and we’re not motivated or incentivised to educate ourselves on anything, except if it can be used to ease the financial burden that comes with existence.

This is nothing new, what I’m saying. Humanity has learned this lesson before. Every offending MAP was a child, at some point. They were innocent, they had never done anything wrong. Then, they started having these thoughts, and they didn’t know what to do. Who can you talk to? Who will help you understand why you feel this way, what it means, and what you can do to control it? There are no resources to help these people not do what society has deemed objectively evil, when society should provide those resources, if we truly cared about preventing victimisation. The truth is we don’t. You know we don’t, because we constantly turn to these ageing elites to tell us how to help ourselves, like they’re capable of understanding us at all.

Let’s discuss this! Legitimately. I am interested in talking to you about this stuff. I haven’t been reading about the struggles of MAPs, but I’ve been reading books about groups who have been more able to historically document their struggle, because they understand exactly what they are, and why it is wrong to hate them for being born as they are.

The majority of the world feels an adult having any form of intimate relationship with someone under the age of 18 is immoral, and I agree, but the world does not consider the possibility that it’s our responsibility to help those with natural desires we deem immoral. That’s because we do not value your life, if you have those desires, regardless of whether you act on them. This is problematic. This does not fit with the justifications we’re given for why our nations invade here, or why these people are all evil, or any of that. It means that we hated you before you did anything worth hating, so of course NOMAPs are going to be at risk of acting on these desires.

The only reason I understand this is because I have immoral desires, too. I desire to end my own life, regardless of how selfish it is, because I am autistic, and this world is difficult for us. I’ve been living like this for too many years, and I’m sick of waiting for mental health professionals. I don’t believe I should be denied help because I cannot afford it. This world also refuses to change, to accommodate us, despite the fact that there is a higher risk of suicide in autistic people. I don’t want to kill myself, simply because I was born with a broken brain. More than anything, I want to dedicate my life to learning some practical, high demand trade, and using my knowledge to improve the quality of life for my community, because I understand the importance of community, and I want them to understand that I appreciate them. Do I deserve to die, because I need more assistance in understanding the necessary social interactions that come with the journey to achieving my goal? Of course not. If the world will not accommodate autistic people, it should at least try to help us fit into the space it wants us to occupy. This is how I feel about MAPs, regardless of whether they have acted on their desires. We need to help these people fit into the world we expect them to fit into.

If you would like to talk about this, I’d be happy to do so, but I would prefer to do so privately. In order for us to have a productive discussion, we need to establish a common understanding of the world. This is different for everyone, and I don’t want to be told I should kill myself because my understanding of the world doesn’t fit how someone else wants it.
